note: Phase 02 fills for data/vault/repro/*.json claims[]: tastylive's own value and sources per tested claim (paraphrase only). Matched by claim text and re-applied by zenith.vault.repro.save on every build. Filled 2026-10-25 (user-approved).

fills.claim: Selling premium beats buying it over time
fills.tasty_value: tastylive's core premise: implied volatility often overstates realized, so sellers are paid for the gap (no figure given on the page)
fills.tasty_note: Qualitative on the pages reviewed; the archive's premium-selling studies were not extracted in full.

fills.claim: A short-premium book is a distinct, high-probability return engine for 25-50% of capital
fills.tasty_value: Keep 25-50% of buying power in options, max 75%; skew higher in high volatility and small accounts
fills.tasty_note: Allocation guidance, not a return claim; tastylive does not frame it against the S&P 500.

fills.claim: Defined-risk wings give up much of the edge
fills.tasty_value: A 16-delta condor with 5-delta wings keeps about 60% of the strangle's median P&L with about 38% less tail risk and 2.5x less buying power (SPY, 2005-2021)
fills.tasty_note: Agrees in direction: tastylive also finds the wings cost about 40% of profit.

fills.claim: Buying options or protection loses money over time
fills.tasty_value: Hedge costs (premium) can outweigh the protection and cap upside; hedging suits risk-averse investors
fills.tasty_note: Qualitative; no tastylive figure for the cost of puts found.

fills.claim: Long-volatility positions have no useful role in a portfolio
fills.tasty_value: Low IV rank favors long premium (debit spreads, long straddles); buy when IV rank and VIX are depressed
fills.tasty_note: tastylive gives long volatility a conditional role (low IV), not a hedge role.

fills.claim: Manage risk by trading smaller rather than buying puts
fills.tasty_value: To reduce tail risk, cut position size first, prefer defined risk, and consider 60+ DTE; size each trade under about 5% of the account
fills.tasty_note: Agrees: tastylive's first lever is size, not puts.

fills.claim: After an outlier earnings move, more than half of companies keep drifting in the same direction over the next month (user seed hypothesis)
fills.tasty_note: User seed hypothesis; no tastylive page or checked episode states a post-earnings drift rate. tastylive's earnings stance is to sell the IV crush and avoid directional earnings bets [page:concepts-earnings].

fills.claim: Large-cap drift after earnings is about zero since 2006 (lit:martineau-2022), so the continuation rate for large caps after 2006 should be near 50%
fills.tasty_note: Literature claim; no tastylive source found.

fills.claim: zenith's PEAD tracker picks (SUE + same-signed reaction) keep drifting over ~1 month
fills.tasty_note: zenith's own tracker; not a tastylive claim.

fills.claim: The expected move (about 1 standard deviation; 16-delta strikes) contains the underlying about 68% of the time
fills.tasty_value: About 68% of outcomes fall within 1 SD; a 1-SD (16-delta) strike has about a 16% chance of finishing ITM
fills.tasty_note: tastylive states the normal-theory figure; our test found 83.9% inside the band.

fills.claim: Breaches are asymmetric: the market breaks the downside less often but further (crash risk the sellers are paid for)
fills.tasty_value: Normal equity skew is negative: OTM puts are richer because of hedging demand
fills.tasty_note: tastylive explains the skew; it does not quantify breach asymmetry.

fills.claim: Sell 16-20 delta strangles at 45-60 DTE and manage at 50% of max profit or ~21 DTE
fills.tasty_value: Sell strangles around 45 DTE at about 16 delta; take profit at 50% of the credit or manage at about 21 DTE
fills.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.

fills.claim: Managing winners at 50% of max profit improves results
fills.tasty_value: Close winners at about 50% of max profit: higher win rate, capital freed to redeploy, better P&L per day
fills.tasty_note: The managing-winners page gives no resulting figure.

fills.claim: Exiting at 21 DTE reduces tail losses
fills.tasty_value: Closing at 21 DTE cut the worst-5% loss by 46% in SPY and 40-60% across four ETFs vs holding (2006-2023)
fills.tasty_note: tastylive's figure is larger than our model's (about a third).

fills.claim: Management rules increase the strategy's expected edge
fills.tasty_value: Managing early (50% or 21 DTE) at about 45 DTE gave the best results in both high and low IV; early profit-taking described as an advantage beyond the volatility premium
fills.tasty_note: Measured on win rate, standard deviation and return on buying power, not on expected edge per unit of risk.

fills.claim: Avoid hard stop-losses on short premium
fills.tasty_value: Close a losing premium-selling trade at a net loss of 2x the credit received (described as optimal in tastylive research)
fills.tasty_note: Note the tension: the claim says 'avoid hard stops', while this tastylive page recommends a 2x-credit exit.

fills.claim: About 45 DTE is the best tenor for selling premium
fills.tasty_value: 45 DTE balances accelerating decay with enough distance to collect premium; lengthen toward 60-65 DTE when IV is low
fills.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.

fills.claim: Allocate more to short premium as VIX rises (sell when volatility is high)
fills.tasty_value: Allocation skews higher in higher volatility (within 25-50% of buying power, max 75%); sell volatility when IV rank is above 50, especially with VIX elevated
fills.tasty_note: The VIX-tiered allocation ladder is not verified from a primary tastylive source (Phase 03 needs-check).

fills.claim: Volatility spikes mean-revert, so short-vol entries after a spike are paid
fills.tasty_value: Traders rely on IV mean reversion: extreme IV tends to normalize, so high IV rank favors short premium
fills.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.

fills.claim: Implied volatility overstates realized volatility most of the time, so selling premium has positive expected value
fills.tasty_value: IV often overestimates realized volatility, a cushion that pays option sellers (no figure given)
fills.tasty_note: Filled in Phase 02 (2026-10-25) from tastylive pages and checked episode extracts.

fills.claim: Sell more premium when IV rank or IV percentile is high
fills.tasty_value: IV rank above 50 favors selling; 80 and above is extreme; 20 or below favors buying
fills.tasty_note: tastylive also warns elevated IV can be justified, so extreme IV rank is not an automatic signal.
